statement: A goal card asked v17 to treat a failed history read "exactly as v27 does today": no composite, no verdict. In the code, v27 withholds the verdict only for a shallow or unknown history depth; on a complete clone whose history read failed (a read limit, the file cap, a partial clone's missing object) it keeps a composite with A2 at 0. Porting the card's description would have invented a v27 behaviour and broken the card's own rule that complete clones stay byte-identical. The session ported what v27's code does, pinned the complete-clone failed-read case as unchanged, and named the rest as left open. Rules: when a card names a reference implementation, read it and measure it on a fixture before porting; port what the code does, not what the card says; where they differ, pin the difference in a test and say so in the handback.
